title: 程序设计的目标和流程

text: What a program is, and the four steps you repeat for every problem.
A program is a list of exact steps that turns the **input** into the required **output**.
A contest problem gives you a statement, the input and output formats, some samples and the limits. Your steps must be right for every allowed input, and fast enough.
Most of your time goes into the last two steps: testing on the samples, then on small cases you make up yourself.
Every C++ program you write will start like this one.

text: A missing `;`, a wrong bracket or a misspelt name is a **compile error**: the program does not run at all. Read the first error message. Its line number points at the mistake, or just after it.
Some problems only ask you to print a fixed picture. Copy it exactly, spaces included.
A raw string `R"(...)"` prints everything between the brackets exactly as typed. It is the easy way through picture problems like P1000, B2025 and B2005.

title: Line by line
rows: Every `int` becomes `long long`, so overflow is rare
`endl` becomes `'\n'`: a newline without the slow flush
Every `double` becomes `long double`: about 18 digits instead of 15
`fast` speeds up cin and cout. After it, never mix them with scanf or printf
`main` must return int, and the macro would break it, so write `signed`
`(double)` makes the sum a long double before dividing, so 3 / 2 gives 1.5

text: The three macros save time, but each one hides a trap.
`#define int long long`: printf needs `%lld`, and the largest value is `LLONG_MAX`, not `INT_MAX`.
`#define double long double`: `printf("%f", x)` silently prints 0.000000. Use `cout << fixed << setprecision(k)` instead.
`#define endl '\n'`: endl no longer flushes. In an interactive problem, call `cout.flush()` after every question you send.
Operators, the order they run in, and two kinds of division.
C++ works out arithmetic like a calculator: brackets first, then `* / %`, then `+ -`. Within one level it goes left to right.

title: The operators
rows: Divide. Two integers drop the fraction

text: Word problems like P2433 小学数学 N 合一 are all this: turn each sentence into one expression, and choose integer or real division on purpose.
Integer division throws the fraction away. It always cuts **toward 0**, even for negative numbers.

text: `pow` returns a double, so a big integer power can be off by one. Multiply in a loop instead. `sqrt` returns a double too.
Check yourself before moving on.
Named boxes that hold values, and values that never change.
A **variable** is a named box that holds one value of a fixed type.
Watch the boxes fill up as a program runs, one line at a time.
To swap two boxes you need a third. Writing `a = b` first would wipe out a.
`swap(a, b)` does the same three moves for you.

text: `=` stores a value, `==` compares two. A variable you never gave a value holds garbage, so always set it before use.
